# Pretraining And Fine-Tuning

Pretraining learns from relationships in a broad collection of records.
Fine-tuning starts from those learned weights and adapts the model to a specific
task. In relflow, both use `trainer.fit(...)`; the data and reconstruction
objectives determine what the model learns.

| Stage | Data | Objectives |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Self-supervised pretraining | Records without task labels | Reconstruct sampled observed values with `rf.Mask(rate=..., reconstruct=True)`. |
| Supervised fine-tuning | Labeled task records | Predict always-hidden labels with `mask=True`, optionally retaining some reconstruction objectives. |
| Resume a run | The same training task | Restore the model, optimizer, scheduler, and loop progress from a full Lightning checkpoint. |

Pretraining is optional. A supervised model can also start from newly
initialized weights. An ordinary float mask, such as `mask=0.15`, only supplies
input dropout; pretraining needs `reconstruct=True` to create an objective.

## Pretrain On Histories

This customer record has no churn label. Purchase amounts and merchant types
provide their own supervision when selected values are hidden:

```yaml
tenure_days: 420
region: northeast
purchases:
  - days_ago: 12
    amount: 42.75
    merchant: grocery
  - days_ago: 3
    amount: 18.50
    merchant: cafe
```

```python
import lightning.pytorch as lit

import relflow as rf

model = rf.Model.md(
    tenure_days=rf.Number,
    region=rf.Category,
    purchases=rf.Branch(
        length=64,
        overflow="tail",
        days_ago=rf.Number,
        amount=rf.Number(mask=rf.Mask(rate=0.15, reconstruct=True)),
        merchant=rf.Category(
            mask=rf.Mask(rate=0.15, reconstruct=True),
        ),
    ),
)
model.optimizer = rf.adamw(learning_rate=1e-3)
pretraining_data = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    model=model,
    train=pretrain_table,
    validate=pretrain_validation_table,
)
pretrainer = lit.Trainer(max_epochs=50)
pretrainer.fit(model=model, datamodule=pretraining_data)
model.save("artifacts/customer-pretrained.rf")
```

The two tables are independent, application-supplied Arrow splits with this
record structure. Histories are sorted oldest to newest for `overflow="tail"`.
Use `rf.PolarsDataModule` with eager frames when the application prepares its
splits in Polars. Keep preparation consistent through the
[preprocessing pipeline](preprocessors.qmd).

Each sampled value is predicted from the remaining context; unselected values
remain inputs. These fractional reconstruction policies also sample during
validation and test, but are inactive during ordinary prediction. See
[Masking](../core-concepts/dynamic-masking.qmd) for selection and stage rules.

The example saves the final model. Use the checkpoint selection described in
[Training](lightning.qmd) to save the best validation state instead.

## Evaluate Vocabulary Coverage

For large-vocabulary reconstruction, report how many selected answers the
model can express as well as how well it predicts them. For example, monitor
`/purchases/merchant/validate.coverage.content` alongside
`/purchases/merchant/validate.nll.content` and
`/purchases/merchant/validate.accuracy.all`.
The [Category metrics](../data-types/category.qmd#vocabulary-and-learning) and
[Cluster metrics](../data-types/cluster.qmd#learning-and-inspection)
define these denominators and count unavailable targets explicitly.

An unknown Category or Cluster target contributes no label gradient. Forcing its
prediction to be uniform over known labels would teach a different task, not
recover the missing answer. With no known targets, conditional reconstruction
quality is `NaN`; zero coverage means the validation objective is unmeasurable,
not that the model reconstructed everything perfectly. Cluster balancing and
adaptive-cluster updates also exclude unknown answers. Do not select a
checkpoint from such a conditional score without checking coverage.

Vocabulary growth can change the evaluated known-target population between
epochs. NLL can increase when newly admitted, difficult labels join it even
if predictions on the old labels improve. The summed validation loss is not a
coverage-adjusted model-quality score. Keep a fixed validation source, monitor
coverage, and compare known-target quality at comparable coverage. If necessary,
retain a fixed cohort of training-established labels for an additional stable
diagnostic; do not populate the model vocabulary from validation or test data.

Random reconstruction masks introduce another source of variation. For a
repeatable diagnostic, supply application-owned Boolean selection fields and
use `Mask(query=..., reconstruct=True)`. This fixes selected coordinates;
it does not freeze vocabulary growth or make unknown answers learnable.
Keep any held-out calibration set separate from model selection, and evaluate
downstream confidence separately for familiar and unseen input identities.

[P062](../proofs/vocabulary/pretraining-coverage.py) isolates vocabulary
coverage with fixed query-selected masks and checks that rebatching the same
targets cannot change the reported counts or conditional scores.
[P065](../proofs/vocabulary/cluster-pretraining-coverage.py) tests Cluster coverage.

[P066](../proofs/vocabulary/rolling-input-admission.py) separately checks cold
Category inputs across successive training cohorts. It currently exposes a
remaining failure: admitting an input identity can change reconstruction NLL
without an optimizer step, even at complete target coverage. Target coverage
does not measure input familiarity. Keep input cohorts separate when assessing
pretraining stability; fixed masks alone cannot remove this source of drift.
Initialization alternatives that pass the admission check have failed other
learning proofs and are not enabled in the model.

[Set metrics](../data-types/set.qmd#vocabulary-and-learning) count positive
memberships rather than scalar targets. A partial-OOV Set retains its known
positive and negative supervision; dropping the whole set would discard valid
evidence. An all-OOV set still supplies known negatives when annotations are
complete. Report member coverage, complete-set coverage, exact-set accuracy,
and micro F1 together. Empty sets are valued, complete annotations, although
an all-empty evaluation has no positive-member denominator. These semantics
are not appropriate for incompletely annotated labels without further masking.

## Adapt To A Labeled Task

For fine-tuning, each customer record gains `churned: false` or `churned: true`,
defined over a future outcome window. Its purchase history ends at the decision
time. Pretraining and fine-tuning splits must respect the same evaluation
boundaries; pretraining on held-out customers or future observations changes
what the downstream evaluation measures.

Load the pretrained artifact, remove its sampled reconstruction policies, and
add a supervised label:

```python
finetuned = rf.Model.load("artifacts/customer-pretrained.rf")
reconstructed_inputs = rf.where("address").is_in(
    [rf.Address("purchases", "amount"), rf.Address("purchases", "merchant")]
)
finetuned.update(reconstructed_inputs, mask=False)
finetuned.extend(
    rf.where("address") == rf.Address(),
    churned=rf.Boolean(mask=True),
)
```

Amount and merchant remain visible inputs. Churn is always excluded from
input embedding, while its observed label supplies the training loss. If the
target already exists in the schema, use `finetuned.update(target, mask=True)`
instead of adding it again.

```{typst}
//| label: fig-pretraining-transfer
//| fig-alt: "Customer context combines tenure, region, and repeated purchases containing age, amount, and merchant. Fine-tuning adds a churn prediction at the customer root."
//| fig-cap: "Pretraining reconstructs selected amounts and merchants. Fine-tuning reuses the customer hierarchy and adds a churn target."
#tree(node("customer", kind: "root", children: (
  node("tenure_days", type: "Number"),
  node("region", type: "Category"),
  node("purchases", kind: "branch", repeated: true, children: (
    node("days_ago", type: "Number"),
    node("amount", type: "Number", detail: "Pretraining objective"),
    node("merchant", type: "Category", detail: "Pretraining objective"),
  )),
  node("churned", kind: "target", type: "Boolean", detail: "Added for fine-tuning"),
)))
```

Schema edits rebuild modules and retain state entries whose names, types, and
tensor shapes still match. The new target starts with newly initialized state;
changing widths, field types, or structure can also reinitialize incompatible
parts. Keep existing addresses and geometry stable when reusing a pretrained
model. Adding a field can change context and reduction behavior even when
existing weights transfer. [Schema Mutation](schema-mutation.qmd) describes
these boundaries.

## Start A New Training Run

Assign a fresh optimizer factory after the edits and use a new Trainer with
labeled Arrow splits. A smaller learning rate is a starting point to evaluate:

```python
finetuned.optimizer = rf.adamw(learning_rate=1e-4)
finetuning_data = rf.ArrowDataModule(
    model=finetuned,
    train=finetune_table,
    validate=finetune_validation_table,
)
finetuner = lit.Trainer(max_epochs=20)
finetuner.fit(model=finetuned, datamodule=finetuning_data)
finetuned.save("artifacts/customer-churn.rf")
```

This starts new optimization from the transferred model state. Use `ckpt_path`
with a full Lightning checkpoint when [resuming the same task](lightning.qmd#resume-training),
including its optimizer and loop progress.
Reapply any processors, scheduler, and desired compilation after loading and
schema edits. For DDP, every rank must construct the same final schema.

Fine-tuning here updates the model end to end, including the new decoder and
existing encoders. Loaded [vocabularies](../core-concepts/vocabulary.qmd) and
Number normalization statistics also
continue learning from training observations; loading does not freeze them.
Validation, test, and prediction reuse that state. For a fixed feature extractor,
set `embed=True` on the desired root or branch, export
[embeddings](../core-concepts/embeddings.qmd) in prediction mode, and fit a
separate downstream model on those vectors.

At inference, omit `churned` from the input and read the prediction at
`/churned`. See [Prediction Output](prediction-output.qmd).

## Keep Auxiliary Objectives Deliberately

To retain amount reconstruction alongside churn, keep that policy when
adapting the pretrained artifact. Replace the earlier
`finetuned.update(reconstructed_inputs, mask=False)` call with:

```python
finetuned.update(
    rf.where("address") == rf.Address("purchases", "merchant"),
    mask=False,
)
finetuned.update(
    rf.where("address") == rf.Address("purchases", "amount"),
    weight=0.1,
)
```

Then add the churn target and start the new run as above. Keeping the amount
policy preserves its trained decoder; removing reconstruction and later
reenabling it creates a new decoder. Both amount and churn losses are now
optimized. `weight` scales the amount loss rather than its sampling rate or a
fixed fraction of the combined loss.

Compare fine-tuning against the same supervised task trained from scratch.
Use the same held-out data and churn metric: pretraining loss and fine-tuning
loss have different objective sets and are not directly comparable. Retaining
auxiliary objectives may help or hurt the task, so evaluate that choice rather
than assuming pretraining guarantees a better model. See [Evaluation](evaluation.qmd).
